[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). [章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

[原文]
Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions
[原文]
The results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds
[原文]
As to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].

candidate.answer:
本文指出，PFI精磨过程中片材抗张强度的提高主要来自细纤维化和细组分的增加，而不是直接来自单根纤维强度的提高。 [1]
细纤维化产生新的表面和更多孔隙，并提高纤维润胀（WRV），使纤维横向更柔顺，从而改善纤维间结合强度。 [1]
零距抗张指数通常用于表征纤维的拉伸强度，因此可用于检查精磨对纤维本体强度的影响。 [1]
本文零距抗张结果表明PFI精磨没有降低纤维强度，这与Kouko等的报道一致。 [1]
因此，本文结论是PFI精磨提高了细纤维化程度、纤维润胀和片材抗张强度，但没有出现纤维拉伸强度的下降。 [1]
零距抗张强度按ISO 15361用Z-Span 2400仪器测定。 [2]

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

claims.text: 本文指出，PFI精磨过程中片材抗张强度的提高主要来自细纤维化和细组分的增加，而不是直接来自单根纤维强度的提高。
细纤维化产生新的表面和更多孔隙，并提高纤维润胀（WRV），使纤维横向更柔顺，从而改善纤维间结合强度。
零距抗张指数通常用于表征纤维的拉伸强度，因此可用于检查精磨对纤维本体强度的影响。
本文零距抗张结果表明PFI精磨没有降低纤维强度，这与Kouko等的报道一致。
因此，本文结论是PFI精磨提高了细纤维化程度、纤维润胀和片材抗张强度，但没有出现纤维拉伸强度的下降。
零距抗张强度按ISO 15361用Z-Span 2400仪器测定。

basis.text: In Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers.

claim_assessments.text: 本文指出，PFI精磨过程中片材抗张强度的提高主要来自细纤维化和细组分的增加，而不是直接来自单根纤维强度的提高。

basis.text: The beating degree and the WRV had a significant increment with increasing PFI refining revolutions, as can be seen in Figure 2. It is caused by the higher fibrillation that produces the new surface and more pores (as shown in Table S1 in Online Resource). The increase in swelling characterized by WRV makes the fibers more compliant in transverse [1], which contributes to improving the inter-fiber bonding strength of the fiber network. The results of fiber morphology analysis and water retention value showing that the fibrillation and the separation between fibrils increase with the refining process.

reference_answer: 作者将纸张抗张性能改善主要联系到细纤维化、细小纤维及纤维间结合。零距抗张指数用于表征纤维本身的抗张强度，结果表明本文PFI处理没有降低纤维强度。因此应区分纸页网络性能和纤维本身强度，不能只凭纸张变强推断单根纤维必然变强。

basis.text: In Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers.

用Savitzky–Golay算法获得导数曲线，并按不同氢键所属波数区间从二阶导数谱确定各氢键组分的峰位。 [1]
对3000–3700 cm⁻¹的羟基伸缩振动区进行非线性拟合，采用Gaussian函数，软件为Peakfit 4.12。 [1]
峰位归属为：3580–3550 cm⁻¹为free OH(2)和OH(6)；3455–3410 cm⁻¹为O(2)H···O(6)分子内氢键；3375–3340 cm⁻¹为O(3)H···O(5)分子内氢键；3310–3230 cm⁻¹为O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键（cellulose I）。 [3]

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds [原文] On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(30) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(30) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1). [章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds [原文] As to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].

PFI 打浆过程中，O(6)H···O(3′)、O(3)H···O(5) 和 O(2)H···O(6) 三种氢键的峰位几乎不变，因此由峰位计算出的氢键能量和氢键距离基本不变。 [1]
但这只说明各类型氢键的局部能量和距离参数稳定；论文摘要同时指出，打浆后各种氢键的含量会发生变化。 [2]
Table 2 显示 softwood 纤维的 O(6)H···O(3′) 相对含量从 0 r 的 28.23% 降至 16,000 r 的 23.56%，而 O(3)H···O(5) 从 28.44% 升至 34.92%。 [3]
总体而言，softwood 和 hardwood 纤维的 O(6)H···O(3′) 含量分别下降 16.54% 和 5.91%，O(3)H···O(5) 含量分别增加 22.78% 和 8.8%。 [1]
游离 OH(2) 和 OH(6) 的含量也随打浆变化，作者将其归因于氢键断裂以及新氢键（如 O(2)H···O(6) 或 O(6)H···O(3′)）的形成。 [3]
O(6)H···O(3′) 含量与 CI-XI 的 Pearson 相关系数为 softwood 0.912、hardwood 0.889（p<0.05），表明氢键含量变化与结晶度变化相关。 [5]

Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

 On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).

As to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].

In the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

As to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].

[原文]
The results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.

[原文]
Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

PFI打浆对纤维的主要作用包括内部细纤维化（细胞壁分层、松弛和润胀）、外部细纤维化（表面微细纤维剥离但仍附着）、纤维切断和细小纤维生成。 [2]
这些作用会提高纤维的可及性、润胀性、柔顺性和纤维间结合能力，从而为成纸强度提高提供基础。 [2]
随PFI转数增加，打浆度和WRV显著升高；文中归因于细纤维化产生新的表面和更多孔隙。 [1]
WRV表征的润胀增加使纤维在横向更柔顺，这有助于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。 [1]
Figure 1显示，PFI打浆后软木浆的纤维长度下降，而细小纤维含量上升，同时宏观细纤维化指数上升。 [1]
PFI打浆提高了细纤维化程度（尤其是内部细纤维化）、纤维润胀和纸页拉伸强度，且零-span结果说明未降低单根纤维强度。 [1]
分子层面，O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键总量在打浆中下降，且更少的分子间氢键和较低结晶指数有利于提高纤维柔顺性、可及性和WRV。 [3]
湿纸幅强度方面，软木浆的增加比硬木浆更显著，作者强调纤维长度对湿纸幅强度起重要作用。 [1]
所给证据没有给出纤维长度、细小纤维和WRV三者对成纸强度贡献的定量排序；从直接论述看，WRV/润胀（内部细纤维化）与纤维间结合强度的联系最直接，而纤维长度主要被强调为湿纸幅强度的关键因素。 [1] [2]

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. [章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds. [章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds [原文] As to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend in general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H· · · O(6) or O(6)H· · · O(30)H-bonds. Thus although there is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6) might disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H· · · O(30) or the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds might increase upon drying.

claims.text: PFI打浆对纤维的主要作用包括内部细纤维化（细胞壁分层、松弛和润胀）、外部细纤维化（表面微细纤维剥离但仍附着）、纤维切断和细小纤维生成。
这些作用会提高纤维的可及性、润胀性、柔顺性和纤维间结合能力，从而为成纸强度提高提供基础。
随PFI转数增加，打浆度和WRV显著升高；文中归因于细纤维化产生新的表面和更多孔隙。
WRV表征的润胀增加使纤维在横向更柔顺，这有助于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。
Figure 1显示，PFI打浆后软木浆的纤维长度下降，而细小纤维含量上升，同时宏观细纤维化指数上升。
PFI打浆提高了细纤维化程度（尤其是内部细纤维化）、纤维润胀和纸页拉伸强度，且零-span结果说明未降低单根纤维强度。
分子层面，O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键总量在打浆中下降，且更少的分子间氢键和较低结晶指数有利于提高纤维柔顺性、可及性和WRV。
湿纸幅强度方面，软木浆的增加比硬木浆更显著，作者强调纤维长度对湿纸幅强度起重要作用。
所给证据没有给出纤维长度、细小纤维和WRV三者对成纸强度贡献的定量排序；从直接论述看，WRV/润胀（内部细纤维化）与纤维间结合强度的联系最直接，而纤维长度主要被强调为湿纸幅强度的关键因素。

The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(30) H-bonds. Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

basis.text: For softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, the macro-fibrillation index and the fiber length had a downward trend, and the fines content has an upward trend for the softwood fibers during PFI refining, as can be seen in Figure 1. The macro-fibrillation index and fiber length of softwood fibers changed significantly. However, two parameters of hardwood fibers had no significant variations relative to softwood fibers. It might be because of the lower refining pressure that was applied in hardwood fibers. The macro-fibrillation index characterizes external macro-fibrillation. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds [原文] On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(30) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(30) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1). [章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds [原文] As to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34]. [章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds [原文] In the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.

As to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend in general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H· · · O(6) or O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>)H-bonds. Thus although there is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6) might disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) or the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds might increase upon drying.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining
[原文]
Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets
[原文]
The fines content, weighted mean length, and macro-fibrillation index of each sample were determined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of dry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT 12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus (Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.

basis.text: In Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers.

candidate.answer:
论文的结论是：PFI精炼提高了纤维细纤维化（尤其是内部细纤维化）、纤维润胀和纸页抗张强度，且未降低纤维本身的抗张强度。 [4]
论文将干纸页抗张强度的提高主要归因于PFI精炼过程中细纤维化和细组分（fines）的增加。 [4]
Figure 3显示，随PFI精炼转数增加，软木和硬木样品的干纸页抗张指数均呈上升趋势。 [2]
所提供证据中的力学性能图仅包含干纸页抗张指数、零-span抗张指数和湿纸幅强度，没有耐破指数或撕裂指数数据。 [1] [2]
因此，无法根据所给证据给出同一批样品的耐破指数和撕裂指数精确数值。 [1] [2]

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions
[原文]
The results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.

[原文]
Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

The results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.

Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

reference_answer: 当前问答库只有PFI论文，尚未收录所指Non-Wood Fibers论文，无法基于当前问答库完成两篇实验数据的比较。需要先把第二篇文献导入问答库。文献数据提取页已有文件也不代表它进入了问答检索库。

adjudication.summary: 正确区分FT-IR拟合r²与预测验证集R²/RMSE，未捏造模型名称。纯资料缺失说明的引用分不适用。

candidate.answer:
提供的文献证据主要讨论 PFI 磨浆对纤维形态、抗张强度、结晶度及氢键的影响，而非纸张抗张预测建模。 [1] [2] [4]
表 2 中的 r²（约 0.9989–0.9996）是氢键分峰/非线性拟合的拟合优度，不是预测模型在验证集上的 R²。 [1]
所给证据中未出现验证集 RMSE，也未给出任何已训练纸张抗张预测模型及其最佳模型名称。 [1] [2] [4]

Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds [原文] On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(30) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(30) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).

Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size [原文] The trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region. [章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. adjudication.summary: 两侧均纠正湿纸幅增幅的错误前提；实际Figure 1还支持针叶木更长，不能仅因文字没有精确长度而否定图文事实。

candidate.answer:
所给证据并不支持“阔叶木打浆后湿纸幅强度增幅高于针叶木”；原文明确说针叶木湿纸幅强度的增加比阔叶木更显著。 [1]
作者将这种差异归因于纤维长度：纤维长度对湿纸幅强度起关键作用。 [1]
阔叶木的 macro-fibrillation index 和纤维长度相对针叶木没有显著变化，原因可能是阔叶木打浆时施加的 refining pressure 较低。 [1]
方法部分给出的 PFI 每 bar 长度作用力为针叶木 3.33 N/mm、阔叶木 1.77 N/mm，表明阔叶木受到的打浆作用较弱。 [2]
打浆会提高 beating degree 和 WRV，细纤维化产生新表面和更多孔隙，并改善纤维网络的 inter-fiber bonding；但这些变化在该研究中未使阔叶木湿纸幅强度增幅超过针叶木。 [1]

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining
[原文]
Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

 On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). As to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining
[原文]
Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

basis.text: In Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers.

因此“PFI打浆把纤维素从I型变成II型”这一前提与所给证据不符，结晶度下降不能用I型向II型转变来解释 [2]
随打浆进行，软木浆的CI-XI和CI-XA分别下降4.66%和15.47%，硬木浆分别下降2.65%和19.4% [2]
表1中软木纤维从0转到16,000转，CI-XI由73.23%降至69.82%、CI-XA由40.46%降至34.20%；硬木纤维CI-XI由75.55%降至73.55%、CI-XA由47.16%降至38.01% [3]
CI随打浆先降后升再降的波动，被解释为机械作用先主要作用于结晶区，随后作用于无定形区并可能发生共结晶，之后结晶区被持续破坏 [2]
结晶度下降的同时，O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键总量在软木和硬木纤维中分别减少16.54%和5.91%，归因于PFI机械作用下纤维素分子链之间的断裂，与内、外细纤维化密切相关 [4]
较少的分子间氢键和较低的结晶度会因分子链活动性提高而进一步提升纤维素纤维的柔顺性、可及性和保水值 [4]
结晶尺寸方面，两种纤维垂直于(200)面的尺寸呈上升趋势（软木4.5 nm升至4.7 nm，硬木4.5 nm升至4.7 nm），而(110)面尺寸波动更大，被解释为水分子更易沿亲水的(110)面渗入，使这些晶面承受更多机械作用 [3] [2]
